novel_features.name: Repurchase last order
novel_features.description: Re-add every line item from your most recent order in one call.
novel_features.rationale: Amazon's UI offers buy-again per-item but not as a batched single-action; only a local-history join across orders + order_items can do it as one command.
novel_features.why_it_matters: When an agent needs to restock the exact same household basket the user ordered last week, this is the one-shot path.

novel_features.name: Dry-run history match preview
novel_features.description: Show the ASIN, title, purchase count, and last-purchased date for a query without writing to the cart.
novel_features.rationale: Local FTS resolution lets us answer 'what would `add X` do?' without touching amazon.com.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Agents can validate a planned reorder before committing — and the user can see why a particular ASIN was picked.

novel_features.name: Most-frequent purchase tiebreak
novel_features.description: When multiple history items match a query, pick the one purchased most frequently (not most recently).
novel_features.rationale: Frequency is a stronger signal than recency for repurchases — the household-stable SKU wins over the one-off experiment.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Deterministic, explainable choice between repeated buys — agents don't surprise the user with a one-off SKU.

novel_features.name: History-only repurchase refusal
novel_features.description: Refuses to add anything that isn't already in your local order history.
novel_features.rationale: Repurchase-only is the safety rail. Every other shopping CLI falls back to 'first search result' when the name is ambiguous — exactly the failure mode this CLI prevents.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Critical for agentic shopping — the LLM can't accidentally buy a brand-new item it picked from search.

novel_features.name: Per-profile DB isolation
novel_features.description: Each Amazon account profile gets its own SQLite history database.
novel_features.rationale: Work history and personal history must never cross-contaminate; per-profile DB is the structural guarantee.
novel_features.example: amazon-pp-cli profiles add work --label 'Work account' && amazon-pp-cli --profile work history import work-orders.jsonl
novel_features.why_it_matters: the user has personal and work Amazon accounts — they have totally different purchase patterns and must not be searched together.

narrative.headline: History-first Amazon reorders from the command line — refuses to buy anything you haven't bought before.
narrative.value_prop: Talks directly to amazon.com using your Chrome session cookies. Sub-second add-to-cart, no Playwright running at runtime. Repurchase-only by design — the LLM can't invent a new SKU. Multi-account support via --profile for personal + work.
narrative.auth_narrative: Amazon has no public buyer API. amazon-pp-cli imports your Chrome session cookies (via kooky, or a Cookie-header paste, or a Chrome cookies.json export) and replays HTTP against amazon.com.

quickstart.comment: Create a profile so per-account history stays isolated.
Import cookies from Chrome via kooky.
Verify auth, DB, and amazon.com reachability.
Backfill order history from the browser-side dumper.
Preview which past purchase a query would resolve to.
Actually add the resolved ASIN to the cart.

troubleshoots.fix: Fall back to `amazon-pp-cli auth paste` and paste a Cookie header copied from DevTools.

troubleshoots.symptom: add refuses with 'no match in history'
troubleshoots.fix: Run `amazon-pp-cli history search '<query>'` to see what's actually in the local history; if nothing relevant, run `history import` first.
Re-run with `--yes` — this CLI never places an order without an explicit confirmation flag.
Use the companion browser-side dumper to produce a JSONL from /your-orders, then `amazon-pp-cli history import <path>`.

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for this when an agent or human user wants to restock a previously-purchased item from Amazon and you want a guarantee the agent cannot drift into a new SKU. Not for new-item discovery, not for digital downloads, not for returns — only repurchase.
